intro: Picture taking the kids to the beach and it starts raining — but they can still play all day because there's an indoor playground in the same building as your room — Balcony Seaside Sriracha Hotel & Serviced Apartments is a seaside resort and serviced apartment in the Bang Phra area of Si Racha that pitches itself specifically as a stay for families with children · the heart of the place is Mini Harborland, an indoor playground with slides, a ball pit, small sports courts, a rope-climbing tower, Sky Bike, and Laser Wars, plus pools, a gender-separated Japanese-style ofuro, and a seaside sand-play zone · rooms come with in-room kitchens, from Studios up to two-bedroom suites of around 95 sqm that suit big families · prices start at about THB 4,000/night · scored 9.1 from 116 reviews on Trip.com, and in the 9.0 Wonderful band on Agoda

body.html: Overview and who it's for — the shortest way to put it is that Balcony Seaside Sriracha is one of the most clearly designed "families with kids" stays on the Chon Buri side · it isn't a quiet luxury resort selling romance for couples, and it isn't a stylish design stay built for photos — it's a large 4-star resort and serviced apartment on the waterfront in the Bang Phra area of Si Racha, open since 2013 and majorly renovated in 2016 · it has as many as around 234 rooms across several buildings, and most importantly it has Mini Harborland, an indoor playground built into the property, so the kids have somewhere to play all day even when it rains or the sun is fierce · real reviews line up on this: the people it suits best are families with young children up to primary-school age who want their kids to run around safely all in one place, without having to drive off to find things to do far away · another group that says they were impressed is large multi-generational families travelling in a big group, because the rooms have kitchens and are spacious enough to stay in together comfortably · on the flip side, if you're a couple after peace and quiet, or a traveller who wants a central location for strolling between cafes, this may not be your answer, because the main atmosphere is lively with the sound of children and activity · put simply, Balcony Seaside sells itself as a "stay that's a destination in itself" for families, rather than just a bed to crash in along the way

Location and getting there — Balcony Seaside sits in Bang Phra subdistrict of Si Racha District, on a fairly quiet seafront road a little way out from the bustle of central Si Racha · the upside of this location is that it's right on the sea and has a genuine bayside feel while still being very easy to reach from Bangkok — take the motorway or Bang Na–Trat down and you're there in about an hour and a half to two hours, which makes it great for a family weekend trip when you don't want to drive all the way to Pattaya · from the hotel it's about a 10–15 min drive into central Si Racha with its Japanese restaurants and markets, about 15 min to Ko Loi and the Si Racha market, and about 30–40 min down to North Pattaya, so you can use it as a base for both the Si Racha side and Pattaya · nearby nature spots like Bang Phra Reservoir, Si Racha Tiger Zoo, and Khao Khiao are also a short drive away · the one thing to say straight from real reviews is that the property isn't in an area where you can walk out to anything — there aren't many restaurants or convenience stores within walking distance, so having your own car is the most convenient · people without a car can still stay, since almost all the activities are at the property anyway, but you should plan ahead for getting food beyond the breakfast

"Brought our two kids, booked two nights and barely had to go anywhere. The kids played at Harborland morning and afternoon, swam in the evening, and we parents got to soak in the ofuro and relax. The room had a kitchen so we could warm milk and food for the kids. Great value for the price — we'll be back next time."

Room types and decor — Balcony Seaside has around 234 rooms across several buildings, and every room is a serviced apartment with its own kitchenette, which is where families rate it highly · the entry-level room is a Studio that combines the bedroom and sitting area in one, around 40 sqm, stepping up to the Family Superior Suite Corner of around 55–59 sqm with a big bed for the parents and a bunk bed for the kids, plus a corner window that in some rooms looks out to the sea · the largest is the two-bedroom Luxury Suite of around 95 sqm with a master bedroom with an en-suite bathroom, a second bedroom, and a wide sitting area, suited to big families or two families together · the decor leans toward the warm tones of a family stay rather than a designer look, focused on being genuinely usable · what guests mention often is the kitchen that actually works — with a fridge, microwave, and kettle, so warming milk, warming food, or preparing meals for young kids is easy · many bathrooms have separated wet and dry zones and a bathtub, which the kids love · most reviews praise the rooms as spacious, clean, and comfortable to sleep in · but there's an honest note too: some rooms are starting to show their age given how long the place has been open, some decor looks older than the photos on the booking sites, and some non-seafront rooms look out onto a building or feel rather enclosed, so you should specify a sea-view room when booking if it matters to you

Facilities, pools, and Harborland — this is the main reason people choose to stay at Balcony Seaside · the number-one highlight is Mini Harborland, an indoor playground built into the property and free for staying guests · inside there are slides, a ball pit, small football and basketball courts, a Laser Wars zone for team laser tag, the Seaside Tower rope-climbing tower, and Sky Bike, a sky bike you pedal along an elevated track · the upside families love most is that the kids can play even when it rains or the sun is fierce, with no worries about the weather · there are also indoor and outdoor pools with a kids' pool and inflatable toys and a seaside sand-play zone that mimics a sandy beach where kids can dig and play safely · for the adults there's a gender-separated Japanese-style ofuro and sauna, a gym, and a massage room, so parents can relax while the kids play · there's free parking, meeting rooms, and free Wi-Fi everywhere · to be honest, the point many reviews flag is that the sea in front of the property isn't really swimmable because it's a shallow, muddy-sandy inner-bay shore rather than a white-sand, clear-water beach — some compare it to a sandbox more than open sea · so if you're hoping to swim in the sea properly, this place is better for its pools and activities than for the sea itself

Food and breakfast — Balcony Seaside has a main restaurant serving an international buffet breakfast spanning Thai, Western, and Japanese, and what families talk about a lot is that there's a dedicated food and dessert corner for kids, including ice cream the kids love · many reviews praise the variety of the menu and the easygoing atmosphere that suits young children · one thing to know is that some sources note breakfast may be charged separately from the room rate on certain packages, so check the conditions when booking to see whether the rate includes breakfast · for other meals, the upside of having a kitchen in the room is that you can buy things and cook or reheat them, which helps a lot for families with young kids · but because the location isn't in a restaurant district, some reviews flag that the food options at the property and around it are fairly limited — if you don't want to eat at the hotel every meal, you should drive into central Si Racha, which has plenty of Japanese restaurants and seafood spots to choose from · overall the food here does well on the family breakfast, but it isn't somewhere you'd come mainly to eat your other meals at the property; the flexibility of having your own kitchen makes up for a lot if you're staying several nights

Service and staff — service is another point that gets fairly consistent praise in real reviews · many people write that the staff are friendly, attentive, and good with kids — helping explain how to use the rides at Harborland and helping with extra beds and items for children · there are international reviews impressed to the point of recounting that the laundry service was done for free and returned neatly, and that there's free tea, coffee, and snacks in the lobby, which reflects a genuine effort to look after guests · many staff can communicate in English, so international families can stay with ease · but to be straight about it, because this is a large property with lots of family guests, during long holidays or busy festival periods when it's full, service at some points can slow down and there can be queues for the popular activities — especially Sky Bike and the rope-climbing tower, which run in timed sessions · overall service is still a strength and one of the reasons the review scores stay high

What real reviews say (praise and gripes) — pulling from Trip.com, Agoda, Booking.com, Tripadvisor, and Thai travel blogs, the picture is fairly consistent · on the praise side: it's a stay for families with kids where the activities are packed all in one place, Mini Harborland can be played all day even in the rain, the rooms are spacious with in-room kitchens that suit families and long stays, the breakfast is varied and has a kids' corner, the Japanese-style ofuro lets the adults relax, the staff are friendly and good with kids, and the location is a short drive from Bangkok · on the gripes side: the most-mentioned point is that the sea in front of the property isn't really swimmable, a shallow muddy-sandy shore more like a sandbox than open sea · next is that some buildings and rooms are starting to age given the opening year and some decor looks less new than the photos, some areas inside the building feel rather narrow and enclosed, food options around the property are limited if you don't have a car, and the popular activities have queues when it's busy · most of these gripes are things you can accept once your expectations are set right, rather than big problems, because the main target group is families coming for the activities at the property, not mainly to swim in the sea — and the overall score stays consistently high

"The place is packed with rides — the kids were happy the whole trip, and the room was clean with a kitchen. The one gripe is that the sea in front of the hotel isn't swimmable, it's a shallow beach; if you really want to swim in the sea you have to drive down to Pattaya. But if you come for the kids to play at Harborland and the pools, it's more than worth the price."

Price comparison and value — room rates start at about THB 4,000/night for a Studio on weekdays, rising to around THB 5,000–6,000 for the Family Superior Suite Corner with a bunk bed, up to around THB 7,000–9,000+ for a large two-bedroom suite or during long holidays and festivals · what makes Balcony Seaside good value for families is that the room rate includes entry to Mini Harborland and almost all facilities for free — and given that a typical indoor playground charges per head anyway, the kids being able to play unlimited all day during the stay saves a lot · once you divide the price per head for a family staying in a big room with several people, it works out even better value than paying separately for the stay and for activities · compared with family resorts on the Pattaya side that have water parks or kids' activities, Balcony Seaside usually has the edge on price and on being closer to Bangkok · in short, if you weight bringing the kids to play all in one place, every baht spent comes back as good value — but if you're hoping for white sand, clear water, and a luxury-resort atmosphere, the value drops, because that's not what this place is selling

Things to know before booking — there are several things that help make the stay smoother · one, the sea in front of the property is a shallow beach that isn't really swimmable, so if you want to swim in the sea, plan to drive down to Pattaya Beach or Jomtien Beach and use Balcony Seaside as a base for the activities at the property instead · two, popular activities like Sky Bike and the rope-climbing tower run in timed sessions (morning and evening) — check the schedule and arrive early to avoid long queues on busy days · three, check the package conditions for whether breakfast is included, as some rates may charge breakfast separately · four, if a sea view matters to you, specify a seafront room when booking, since some rooms look out onto a building or feel rather enclosed · five, the building has been open since 2013, so set your expectations around the room size, the in-room kitchen, and the activities rather than brand-new decor · six, driving yourself is the most convenient since there are no shops within walking distance of the property, and there's free parking · seven, during long holidays and school breaks it gets very busy with families, and rooms and activities fill up fast, so book ahead and compare prices across several platforms

The verdict — from everything in the real reviews, Balcony Seaside Sriracha Hotel & Serviced Apartments is the stay that suits families with young children up to primary-school age who want their kids to play all in one place, on an affordable budget and close to Bangkok · Mini Harborland, an indoor playground that works in any weather, the pools, the Japanese-style ofuro, the sand-play zone, and serviced-apartment rooms with in-room kitchens make it a good-value, convenient family stay for a weekend trip · but you have to accept honestly that the sea in front of the property isn't really swimmable, some buildings and rooms are starting to age, the location has no shops within walking distance so it suits people with a car, and the atmosphere is lively with the sound of children all day · if you're a couple after peace and quiet, or you want white sand and clear water to swim in fully, this may not be your answer, and you should consider a beachfront resort on the Pattaya or Jomtien side instead · but for a family trip set on bringing the kids to play to their hearts' content all in one place, close to Bangkok, without paying a lot — Balcony Seaside meets that need well, and that's why it's still one of the first names families think of when it comes to a kid-friendly stay in the Si Racha area

honestSummary: Balcony Seaside Sriracha is the best choice for families with young children up to primary-school age who want their kids to play all in one place, on an affordable budget, close to Bangkok — Mini Harborland indoor playground, pools, a Japanese ofuro, and rooms with in-room kitchens · but you have to accept that the sea in front of the property isn't really swimmable, some buildings have been aging since 2013, and the location has no shops within walking distance so it suits people with a car
honestChecks: If you want white sand and clear water to swim in the sea fully — the sea in front of the property is a shallow, muddy-sandy sandbox-style shore that isn't really swimmable → if swimming in the sea is the priority, plan to drive down to Pattaya–Jomtien beaches, or choose a beachfront resort on that side instead

If you're a couple after peace and quiet — this is a family stay that's lively with the sound of children and activity all day → if you want a calm, romantic atmosphere, consider a boutique resort or an adults-oriented stay instead

If you need a brand-new room and a walkable location — the building opened in 2013 and some spots are starting to age, and there are no shops within walking distance of the property → set your expectations around the activities, the in-room kitchen, and the space, and have a car ready for going out to find food

faqTitle: Frequently Asked Questions — Balcony Seaside Sriracha Hotel & Serviced Apartments

faq.q: Where is Balcony Seaside Sriracha, and is it far to drive from Bangkok?
faq.a: The hotel is located in Bang Phra subdistrict, Si Racha District, Chon Buri province, on the seaside · driving from Bangkok via the motorway or Bang Na–Trat takes about an hour and a half to two hours · it's about 10–15 min into central Si Racha and Ko Loi, and about 30–40 min down to North Pattaya Beach · there aren't many shops within walking distance of the property, so having your own car is the most convenient

faq.q: What's at Balcony Seaside's Mini Harborland, and is it free to play?
faq.a: Mini Harborland is an indoor playground built into the property that staying guests can play at for free · it has slides, a ball pit, small football and basketball courts, a Laser Wars team laser-tag zone, the Seaside Tower rope-climbing tower, and a Sky Bike sky bike · the highlight is that kids can play all day even when it rains or the sun is fierce · some activities run in timed sessions, so check the schedule first

faq.q: What's the starting price at Balcony Seaside Sriracha, and what room types are there?
faq.a: Prices start at about THB 4,000/night for a Studio of around 40 sqm on weekdays · there's the Family Superior Suite Corner (~55–59 sqm with a kids' bunk bed) from around THB 5,500, and the two-bedroom Luxury Suite (up to ~95 sqm) for big families · every room has an in-room kitchen · during long holidays and school breaks the prices rise and rooms fill up fast, so compare several platforms before booking

faq.q: Can you swim in the sea in front of Balcony Seaside?
faq.a: The sea in front of the property is a shallow, muddy-sandy inner-bay shore that isn't really swimmable — better for sitting and taking in the view and letting the kids play in the sand · the property has indoor and outdoor pools with a kids' pool to swim in instead · if you really want to swim in the sea, you should drive down to Pattaya or Jomtien beaches, about 30–40 min away

faq.q: Who is Balcony Seaside Sriracha best suited for?
faq.a: It's very well suited to families with young children up to primary-school age who want their kids to play all in one place, on an affordable budget and close to Bangkok · there's Harborland, pools, an ofuro, a sand-play zone, and rooms with in-room kitchens · it isn't suited to couples after peace and quiet, or people who want white sand and clear water to swim in fully, who should consider a beachfront resort on the Pattaya–Jomtien side instead

faq.q: Does Balcony Seaside have an ofuro and breakfast?
faq.a: Yes · a gender-separated Japanese-style ofuro and sauna for the adults to relax while the kids play · breakfast is an international buffet spanning Thai, Western, and Japanese, with a food and dessert corner for kids including ice cream · check when booking whether the package includes breakfast or charges it separately
